Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Atul Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Varun Kumar Agnihotri, learned Brief Holder for the State and perused the record.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 68 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366A, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, Police Station- Cantt, District- Prayagraj, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: F.I.R. of the present case was lodged against unknown person under Section 363 IPC and according to F.I.R. on 29.3.2022 the minor daughter of the informant aged about 15 years had gone somewhere and she also taken her mobile phone.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits applicant was not named in the F.I.R. but when the victim was recovered and her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded then she stated that on the enticement of the applicant she had gone with him and thereafter on 1.4.2022 they performed marriage.

sentences.text:
He further submits the allegation of enticement made against applicant in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. is totally false and it appears that investigating officer on his own recorded this fact in the statement as when the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
then she did not make any such allegation of enticement against applicant and stated that when applicant asked her about her age then she stated her age to the applicant as 18 years and thereafter she had gone with applicant to Punjab and after that they performed marriage and started living as husband and wife and, therefore, from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. applicant neither enticed away nor abducted the victim and he under the impression had gone with her that she is a major girl aged about 18 years.
He further submits as per school leaving certificate of victim her date of birth is 1.1.2007 and according to that she was around 16 years of age.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. victim specifically stated that when applicant made query about her age then she informed him that her age is 18 years.
I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and peruse the record of the case.

On the perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that she, according to her own wish, had gone along with applicant although in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she stated that applicant enticed her that if she will go with him then he will perform marriage with her and further applicant has performed marriage with her and they started living as husband and wife.

Although, according to the school certificate, age of the victim is around 16 years and, therefore, she appears to be minor i.e. below 18 years of age but from perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that when victim was ready to depart with applicant then he made specific query from her about her age and she informed that her age is 18 years and thereafter applicant and victim had gone and performed marriage and started living as husband and wife.
Therefore, from the discussion made above after considering the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Buddh Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
